items.label: f10-practice-ladder
items.front: 05-PRACTICE: what are exercises 0 to 6, and what are the stretch steps?
items.back: 0 predict the sample orders' totals before running anything; 1 SKU uniqueness; 2 startup-failure exit behaviour; 3 status input parsing at the boundary; 4 catalog repricing with stable line snapshots (menu 15); 5 deleting DRAFT orders only (menu 16); 6 optimistic versions in the domain plus an injected Clock. Stretch (design only): an HTTP contract, transactional persistence, inventory with an outbox, and ownership on every lookup.

items.label: f08-owns-many-config
items.front: Write the EF Core model configuration the C# order sketch uses for its lines and money columns.
items.back: modelBuilder.Entity<Order>().OwnsMany(o => o.Items, b => { b.ToTable("OrderItems"); b.WithOwner().HasForeignKey("OrderId"); b.Property(i => i.UnitPrice).HasPrecision(18, 2); }); plus Property(o => o.DiscountAmount).HasPrecision(18, 2).

items.label: f06-trace-lab-method
items.front: Trace lab set-up: how do you start, and which records do you create before tracing?
items.back: Run the app with -DataPath pointing at a new directory (data/trace-orders). Create a customer with menu 1 (a learning address such as learner@example.test; no email is sent), an active Notebook product with menu 3 (SKU NOTE, price 10.00), and an order with menu 5 for that customer, recording each ID. IDs connect the records; names are display values, not reliable lookup keys.

items.label: f07-regression-inventory
items.front: Which regression tests does the worked change point you to, and where do they live?
items.back: In test/oms/RegressionTests.java: the saved-discount reload case, complete paid restoration, the failed quantity reduction, missing customer/product reference rejection, and the legacy four-file migration. The suite also covers detached copies, status guards, codec escapes, snapshot corruption and failed replacement.

items.label: f04-footer-limits
items.front: What does the count footer in oms.snapshot.txt detect, and what does it not?
items.back: A mismatch detects ordinary truncation or missing records. It is not a checksum and does not resist intentional edits that also change the counts.

items.label: f02-transition-graph
items.front: Give the order status transition graph.
items.back: DRAFT to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED; SUBMITTED to PAID or CANCELLED; PAID to SHIPPED or CANCELLED. SHIPPED and CANCELLED are terminal. Cancelling from PAID is a local status change only; there is no refund integration.

items.label: f03-what-is-still-missing
items.front: The aggregate, the snapshot validation and the atomic file save each protect something. What do none of them provide?
items.back: Authenticated ownership, concurrent request handling, cross-process stale-write detection, and payment idempotency. Those are the next lessons when the CLI becomes a web application.

items.label: f05-csharp-entity-sketch
items.front: The C# Order sketch: how are status, state changes, lines and money totals expressed?
items.back: enum OrderStatus { Draft, Submitted, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }. Every property has a private setter, so state changes only through methods. Lines live in a private List<OrderItem> exposed as IReadOnlyList Items, because the aggregate root owns its lines. Subtotal is a computed property summing each line's LineTotal; nothing about the totals is stored.

items.label: f09-corruption-trace-procedure
items.front: Trace lab: what is the procedure for the corruption trace?
items.back: Exit, copy the learning directory to a fresh, unused destination, append a line after the count footer in the copied oms.snapshot.txt, record Get-FileHash, start the app on the copy, then record the hash again and compare. Keep the valid source directory as the recovery copy and never delete an authoritative snapshot from real learning work to force a fallback.

items.label: f01-derived-totals
items.front: How are subtotal and total computed in the delivered Order, and why?
items.back: getSubtotal sums the current line totals and getTotal subtracts the discount. Deriving them leaves fewer facts to keep in sync; each OrderItem still keeps its own line total, maintained by its quantity method.

items.prompt: Why does FileDataStore rebuild orders with Order.restore instead of creating a DRAFT and replaying addOrMergeItem and setStatus?

items.explanation: 02-CONCEPTS: restoration is not applying user commands. Replaying addOrMergeItem on a loaded order goes through the edit rules (ensureEditable) and touch(), so a saved non-editable order or its update time would not come back as saved. restore builds the complete aggregate and validates it directly.
